output.rationale: E-01 shows 2 of 3 rejects are LOC_UNKNOWN, indicating missing location data as a major issue; E-02 reflects stakeholder view of carrier flakiness but the root cause is shipper data quality (H-SHIPPER-DATA-QUALITY). Providing location reference data targets this cause. The monitoring work item uses the catalog query to track reject reasons over time, enabling measurement of improvement against success criteria SC-LOC-UNKNOWN-TARGET and SC-NO-LOCATION-REJECTS. No protected actions are required as the release scope contains none and there are no mutating tools defined. Side effects include additional effort for the shipper to maintain and consume the reference data and modest storage overhead for the reference dataset. These changes are reversible: the reference data can be withdrawn or versioned and the monitoring query can be stopped without lasting impact. Alternatives considered but not selected include the requested solution of auto‑fixing and resubmitting rejected notices, and repeatedly resubmitting all notices to exploit perceived carrier flakiness; both lie outside the agreed release scope and introduce higher operational risk or unverified assumptions.

The release provides location reference data to the shipper (SH-REQ) and enables monitoring of reject reasons via the carrier reject log (DA-REJ)【DA-REJ】. The define gate resulted in CONDITIONAL_PASS, deferring the unknown whether missing location is dominant vs event order (U-UNK-01, VOB-U-UNK-01) and noting that EVENT_ORDER rejects may persist, so the release proceeds with known limitations【U-UNK-01】【VOB-U-UNK-01】.
